Dedicated capacity pilot vs hosted burst
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes

Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark (Triton CTO), Lena (Triton Head of Platform), Samir (SRE), Hannah (Procurement)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in today, I'll run the agenda — capacity uplift, region add, and next steps for the contract amend. how's everyone's morning?
[00:18] Mark: morning, all good. had a quick sync with infra before this, so hoping we can lock a plan today.
[00:28] Priya: great, we'll start with capacity numbers and then go into the EU onboarding plan. i pulled the recent telemetry, there were some small blips last thurs during the promo spike.
[00:38] Lena: yes i saw that, p95 jumped up to about 380ms for generation endpoints, not huge but outside our target of 250ms.
[00:49] Samir: and we hit queue depth higher than expected, that's why we asked about dedicated pools again — to get predictable throughput.
[01:02] Alex: understood. our proposal was a 20% uplift on reserved capacity, plus adding an EU cluster with cross-region fallback. the amendment would be for a 12 month term extension to cover provisioning lead time.
[01:18] Mark: what's the lead time for EU activation if we go dedicated? we need to know ramp timing for our release in mid-october.
[01:26] Priya: typical provisioning for Dedicated in EU is 2-3 weeks after signed amendment, but if you want a private VPC/onprem path that can be longer. for dedicated reserved pools we can fast track to ~14 days if the sku inventory is available.
[01:45] Lena: ok 14 days is reasonable. any constraints on model sizes or quantization differences between US and EU clusters? we run several quantized 8-bit variants.
[01:57] Priya: vehicle — sorry i mean, yes, same model variants supported; the runtime picks kernels per hardware. you'll see slight perf delta depending on instance family. we'll surface the model profile in the benchmark report.
[02:16] Mark: are there cost delta considerations for EU traffic? our compliance folks want to keep EU data in-region.
[02:23] Alex: cost's slightly higher in EU due to region pricing, and there may be egress considerations. we can present both-hosted route and a dedicated-in-region route; the dedicated in-region typically has higher committed cost but lower per-token spot costs due to stable utilization.
[02:43] Hannah: on the contract side, procurement asked for standard PO language and confirmation of SOC2 scope. can you confirm?
[02:51] Alex: yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, we can share the attestation. for SSO we support SAML and SCIM provisioning; for key management we integrate with external KMS, you can control keys. we'll send the security pack.
[03:08] Samir: how is audit log retention handled for Private customers? we need 12 months of immutable logs for our audits.
[03:16] Priya: audit logs can be routed to your SIEM; retention is configurable on Private deployments. for hosted we have standard retention windows but can extend with an add-on. we'll include exact retention SLAs in the security doc.
[03:35] Mark: good. let's talk pilot — we'd like a short Dedicated pilot for the EU region to validate latency and throughput before fully committing. 2 weeks?
[03:44] Alex: absolutely. we typically recommend a 10-business-day pilot with real traffic replay and a small subset of production traffic. instrumented with tracing and token-level cost.
[03:56] Priya: i'll run the runbook: collect traffic replay, define P95 targets, run continuous batching scenarios. Samir, can you share the representative traffic trace?
[04:05] Samir: yes i'll drop it in the doc repo after this call.
[04:10] Lena: what's the expected P95 improvement if we move to dedicated? i want to set realistic goals.
[04:16] Priya: typically p95 improves 10-30% depending on burst patterns because of continuous batching and reserved kernels; exact numbers we'll provide after the first benchmark and we can tune batching.
[04:28] Mark: any gotchas for our inference stack? we're on k8s + envoy edge, and we do KV cache warming on deploy.
[04:36] Priya: sounds good; Redwood has prefix/KV cache support and the runtime handles warm starts. with your caching pattern we should see steady-state improvement. envoy in front is fine — we'll provide header-level routing suggestions.
[04:50] Alex: okay on pricing — given the 20% uplift and EU add, i've prepared a revised pricing sheet. baseline committed monthly cost goes up ~18% but blended per-token cost will drop assuming 75% utilization.
[05:06] Hannah: what about flexibility if utilization doesn't hit that target in Q1? can we negotiate a scaling clause?
[05:14] Alex: yes, we can include a one-time true-up after 90 days and an option to convert to burst credits. we'll put specific thresholds in the SOW.
[05:25] Mark: and rollback or fallbacks? we need automatic fallback to a compatible hosted model in other regions if capacity is temporarily impacted.
[05:33] Priya: smart routing supports fallbacks by policy; we can pin a cheaper model variant and fallback to a hosted region with cross-region latency considerations. that will be in the operations playbook.
[05:46] Samir: latency numbers on cross-region fallback? approximate?
[05:49] Priya: cross-region adds typically 60-120ms more depending on region. we'll include measured samples during the pilot.
[05:58] Alex: for next steps, i'll send the SOW and the updated pricing sheet. Priya will share the benchmark runbook and a sample latency report. Mark will share traffic profile. Hannah will confirm procurement timeline.
[06:12] Mark: quick question on data residency: does the EU cluster handle logs separately or do they replicate back to the US?
[06:19] Priya: no replication back to US unless you opt in. data-in-region stays in-region for Dedicated Private clusters — we'll confirm exact replication settings in the security pack.
[06:34] Hannah: also need to confirm KMS flow — our security team wants customer-managed keys and envelope encryption.
[06:41] Priya: supported. we have integrations with AWS KMS and other providers; we'll add flow diagram to the docs.
[06:50] Mark: any blockers from Redwood side to start pilot asap?
[06:55] Alex: only signed amendment and a small environment questionnaire. provisioning starts after those.
[07:03] Samir: timeline check — if we sign by next Tues, can we have EU pilot live by Oct 7?
[07:09] Priya: yes that aligns with the 2-week provisioning window.
[07:15] Lena: perfect.
[07:18] Alex: ok, before we close, any competition concerns? we've heard Triton was also evaluating CloudEndpointX.
[07:24] Mark: yes, they pitched a cheaper pay-as-you-go but no multi-region SLA and no private VPC option. it's more of a stopgap.
[07:33] Alex: noted. we'll highlight our SLA and audit controls in the follow-up.
[07:40] Hannah: procurement asks that final SOW include indemnity language and a data processing addendum.
[07:46] Alex: we'll include that and flag to legal.
[07:50] Priya: last technical note — we'll make sure the benchmark includes cold-start scenarios and KV-cache warm runs.
[07:58] Mark: thanks, that's it from us.
[08:02] Alex: great, recap then: Alex send SOW & pricing by 2026-09-24; Priya sends benchmark runbook by 2026-09-23; customer shares traffic profile by 2026-09-22; procurement sends PO timeline/questions by 2026-09-27. pilot to start once amendment signed, target EU pilot live by 2026-10-07.
[08:22] Lena: that matches our expectations. thanks everyone.
[08:26] Alex: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links to the security pack and runbook. bye.

Notes/References:
- Security pack link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (to be sent)
- Benchmark runbook template: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/runbook-template (Priya will populate)
- Pricing sheet (draft) attached in follow-up email

End of transcript.
